description:
FILED + FIXED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07) while bisecting #1061's CPAN-board down-movers.

THE BUG.  The "import PACKAGE" statement sugar (Pl/Parser.pm, _process_expression_statement's two-Word special case) lowered to

    (funcall (intern "PL-IMPORT" :$pkg))

with $pkg interpolated RAW.  A single-segment name survives that (`:threads`
reads as the package the runtime makes for perl's `threads`), but a
MULTI-SEGMENT one produces `:threads::shared` -- not a CL token at all.  SBCL's
reader stops with `too many colons in "threads"`, `load` aborts at that form,
and every form after it in the emitted file is lost, whatever it was.

Pl::Parser::_cl_pkg_designator is the single source of truth for that spelling
-- its own comment says so, and every `in-package`, `p-defpackage` and runtime
package reference already goes through it (it routes to Pl::CLForm::cl_pkg,
which pipe-quotes any name carrying a `:` or a non-ASCII character, #418).
This one site bypassed it.  ONE LINE.

REPRODUCER (perl prints "imported\nafter\n"; PCL before the fix prints nothing
and dies in the reader):

    package My::Mod;
    sub import { print "imported\n" }
    package main;
    BEGIN {
      $INC{'My/Mod.pm'} = 1;
      require My::Mod; import My::Mod;
    }
    print "after\n";

(The BEGIN matters: outside a BEGIN the same statement takes v2's ordinary
method-call lowering, `(p-method-call "My::Mod" "import")`, and is fine.)

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and why it is worth reading.  The CPAN board's
Scalar-List-Utils t/dualvar.t went PARTIAL 14/2 -> FAIL 0/0 between the s378
and s467 snapshots.  The bisect landed on `b95ad912` (s436, Q3, the PHASE
MODEL).  That commit did NOT introduce the bad token -- the s378 tree
(`5d941618`) emits `:threads::shared` too.  What it did was move dualvar.t's
`BEGIN { ... require threads::shared; import threads::shared; ... }` (source
line 72) into the file's compile phase, i.e. AHEAD of the 16 assertions on
lines 11-70 that until then had already run by the time the reader reached the
unreadable form.  A pre-existing silent catastrophe, made visible by a correct
reordering.  "Pre-existing is WHEN, not WHY" cuts both ways.

BARS.  `tools/corpus-diff.pl dfa65afa`: emission IDENTICAL across 111 files,
silent drops 5 unchanged -- so NO generation bump (s470bw's precedent: a
corpus-identical Pl/ change carries main's string).  `tools/emission-ab.pl
--ref dfa65afa --shapes` over lib/ (22 shims + 6 shapes): 28 SAME / 0 DIFF /
0 RCDIFF.  Gate `PCLXS_DIR=~/pclxs tools/prove-core` green.  Guard rows
`Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t` 127 -> 129 (one transpile-shape row asserting
`:|My::Mod|`, one differential run row), inverse-verified on a `dfa65afa`
extraction where BOTH fail -- the run row with the reader error itself.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX.  dualvar.t stays FAIL 0/0 on the board: with the file
readable, its BEGIN now reaches `import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0;`, which is
the SAME sugar with an ARGUMENT LIST and is not handled at all -- task #1506.
subject: FIXED s1061: `import Foo::Bar;` emitted the BARE designator `:Foo::Bar`, which is not a CL token ("too many colons") -- the whole emitted file stopped READING there, and every form after it was lost (Scalar-List-Utils t/dualvar.t, 16 rows)
